title: Video by duncanrogoff
author: Duncan Rogoff | AI for Personal Brands
caption:
Comment “AGENT” and I’ll send you the full breakdown.

You don’t need a fancy dashboard to build your own Jarvis.

The real power is the system running underneath it:

🧠 Brain — Hermes
Install the open-source agent harness and connect it to Anthropic with your Claude API key.

📋 Instructions — Markdown file
Write in plain English what the agent does, when it runs, and what “done” looks like for each task.

🛠️ Skills — Claude Skills
Give it specialized skills for:
• Managing your inbox
• Pulling business numbers
• Turning calls into proposals
• Handling repetitive tasks

🔌 Connections — MCP
Connect it to Gmail, Notion, analytics, and other apps so it can actually work inside your existing tools.

💻 Always-on setup
Run it on something like a Mac Mini or old laptop so it can keep running without you constantly opening it.

That’s basically the whole system.

The flashy dashboard is optional. The real Jarvis is the combination of brain + instructions + skills + tools + automation running underneath.

title: Video by drcintas
author: Dr. Alvaro Cintas
caption:
Comment “MODEL” to run a 26 billion parameter AI model on a PC with only 2GB of RAM.

Around 85% of the model stays on the SSD, and only the experts needed for each token get loaded into memory.

At a 4,000 token context, around 14GB of the model is still sitting on the disk.

The trade-off is speed.

It only pushes around 6 tokens a second. The normal MLX version runs at around 80 tokens per second, but it needs 8 to 10GB of RAM.

This setup uses only 2GB. So it’s slower, but it’s running a 26B model on a laptop with 2GB of RAM.
